common_name: Flamingo Glow Mexican Lily (Cream-Variegated, Pink-Blushed Beschorneria)

planting.note: Divide rooted offsets in spring and plant in full sun in lean, sharply drained soil, siting the clump where strong light will hold the cream leaf variegation and pink blush rather than letting it fade to green.

directions: This is a selected sport of Mexican lily prized for broad, arching, blue-green leaves edged in creamy yellow with a soft pink flush along the margins, especially vivid on new growth in cooler months. Like the species it eventually sends up a dramatic, gracefully arching coral-red flower scape reaching 5-7 feet, hung with pendant tubular red and green blooms that draw hummingbirds for weeks. Full sun intensifies both the variegation and the pink cast on the leaf margins, while too much shade causes the plant to green up and lose its distinguishing color. Give it the same lean, fast-draining soil and cold protection below the mid-teens Fahrenheit that the species needs, and propagate only by dividing basal offsets since seed will not come true to the variegated pattern. After the main rosette flowers and dies back, the surrounding offsets carry the clump forward.
